questions.question_text:
A graph of $y = f(x)$ shows tangents drawn at point $A$ (with gradient $m_A = 5$) and at point $B$ (with gradient $m_B = 1$).
Which statement correctly describes the behaviour of the curve at these two points?

options.text: The curve is rising 5 times faster at point $A$ than at point $B$.
The curve is falling at point $A$ and rising at point $B$.
options.why: Both gradient values are positive, so the curve is rising at both points.

options.text: The curve reaches its maximum at point $A$.
options.why: A positive gradient of $5$ indicates the curve is still rising, not at a peak.

options.text: Point $B$ is 5 times steeper than point $A$.
options.why: Reverses the comparison since $5 > 1$.

questions.solution_text: $\text{Since } m_A = 5\text{ and } m_B = 1\text{, both instantaneous rates are positive, and the curve is rising } 5\text{ times steeper at point } A\text{ than at point } B.$

questions.question_text:
A student needs to estimate the gradient of the tangent at $P(3, 7)$ from a graph.
The tangent line passes through $(1, 1)$ and $(5, 13)$.
Which calculation gives the correct gradient?

options.why: Divides the point coordinates $\frac{y}{x}$ instead of computing the rise over run along the tangent.

options.text: $\dfrac{13 - 7}{5 - 3} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$, but only if $(5, 13)$ is on the curve.
options.why: Any two points on the tangent line are valid regardless of whether they lie on the curve.
Inverts the gradient formula by calculating run over rise.

questions.question_text:
A runner's distance–time graph has a tangent drawn at $t = 6\text{ s}$ that passes through $(3, 15)$ and $(9, 63)$, where distance is in metres.
What is the runner's estimated instantaneous speed at $t = 6\text{ seconds}$?

options.why: Calculates the distance change $63 - 15 = 48\text{ m}$ without dividing by time $6\text{ s}$.
Divides total distance $63$ by time $9$ ($\frac{63}{9} = 7$) with an arithmetic error.
Divides $63$ by $6\text{ s}$ instead of using the two points on the tangent line.
Divides coordinate $y = 3$ by $x = 2$ ($3 \div 2 = 1.5$) instead of computing tangent gradient.
States the $y$-value at the point of tangency instead of the gradient.
States the rise between $(0, -5)$ and $(3, 7)$ without dividing by the run of $3$.

questions.question_text:
A bamboo plant's height $H$ in centimetres over $t$ days is plotted on a graph.
The tangent line at $t = 5\text{ days}$ passes through $(2, 6)$ and $(8, 24)$.
What is the estimated instantaneous growth rate at $t = 5\text{ days}$?

options.why: Calculates the height change $24 - 6 = 18\text{ cm}$ without dividing by the $6\text{-day}$ interval.
Divides $24$ by $5\text{ days}$ instead of using the points on the tangent line.
Inverts the run over rise formula ($\frac{6}{18} = 0.33$) or makes an arithmetic error.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ shows a tangent line drawn at $(2, 7)$ passing through $(0, 1)$ and $(4, 13)$.
What is the exact gradient of this tangent line, and what is its equation?

options.why: Divides $7$ by $2$ to guess slope $3.5$ and assumes a line through the origin.
Uses the point $(2, 7)$ incorrectly as the $y$-intercept.
Divides $13 - 1 = 12$ by $2$ instead of the run $4 - 0 = 4$.
